repository_state.notes: Phase 1 Foundation is complete (see .jarvis/phase_completion_records/P001-completion.md): config, observability, permissions, plugin loader, storage, core service, all under jarvis_core/. 24 automated tests exist and pass (pytest), CI now runs them automatically on every push/PR (.github/workflows/ci.yml, D-0013). Security review performed; two findings fixed (D-0014): permission checks now always write an audit row, and the service's loopback-only binding (D-0011) is enforced at the config layer, not just defaulted. No first-party plugins ship yet.

implemented_features: Layered config system (defaults -> YAML file -> env overrides), validated via Pydantic, with enforced loopback-only service.host (jarvis_core/config)
Structured logging to console + rotating file (jarvis_core/observability)
SQLite storage layer with permission_grants and audit_log tables (jarvis_core/storage)
Capability-based permission system: deny-by-default store, tier classification, require() enforcement gate with mandatory (non-optional) audit logging (jarvis_core/permissions)
Plugin manifest schema + directory-based discovery with per-plugin failure isolation (jarvis_core/plugins)
Core HTTP service (FastAPI/Uvicorn, loopback-only, enforced) with /health and /status endpoints (jarvis_core/service)
CI pipeline running pytest on every push/PR (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
verified_features: Config system: 7 automated tests passing (defaults, file override, env override, path resolution, loopback-host enforcement via direct construction/file/env)
Permission system: 10 automated tests passing (deny-by-default, grant/revoke, full-catalog seeding, tier mapping, require() allow/deny paths, audit-log write on both granted and denied checks)
Plugin discovery/registry: 6 automated tests passing (empty dir, missing dir, valid manifest, invalid manifest isolation, no-manifest dir skipped, registry register/get/list)
Core service: 2 automated tests passing (in-process /health and /status), plus one manual real-socket smoke test confirming the service boots, serves real HTTP, and persists a real SQLite file
Phase 1 completion bar (Implementation + Tests + Integration + Documentation + Security review + Verification) met -- see phase_completion_records/P001-completion.md
active_tasks: Phase 3: decide and wire up a first real AI provider integration per ai_provider_spec.md (provider choice and monthly cost ceiling still open, deferred from Phase 1's current_phase.md)
known_risks: Primary device (HP EliteBook 645 G9) has no dedicated GPU, so the local-tier/cloud-tier split (D-0006) is a hard constraint on later phases, not a preference.
No first-party plugins exist yet, so plugin isolation has only been tested against synthetic fixtures, not a real plugin.

Credential storage (D-0012, OS keyring) has no exercised code path yet -- it will be exercised for the first time by Phase 3's AI provider API keys, so that integration should include tests proving keys are never written to config files or logs.
Android integration approach remains open, deferred to Phase 7 -- not blocking for Phase 3.
Specific cloud AI provider(s) to wire up first, and a monthly cost ceiling, remain open -- blocking for starting Phase 3 implementation; needs an owner decision before architecture work begins.
next_actions: Owner decision: which AI provider(s) to wire up first for Phase 3, and a monthly cost ceiling (D-0007/D-0008 already set the multi-provider and no-cost-to-idle requirements this must satisfy).
Phase 3: specification + architecture-impact analysis for the AI provider abstraction, per agent_rules.md's Feature Development Protocol, before implementation begins.
Phase 3: route provider API keys through the D-0012 keyring layer from day one, with a test proving they never land in config files, logs, or the audit log's detail strings.
Separately, and not blocking Phase 3: a first trivial first-party plugin would give the Phase 1 plugin loader real (not just synthetic) exercise -- worth considering opportunistically.
